content:
The correct answer is **C. sequential**.

In sequential project delivery, different aspects and systems of a building are designed and implemented in a sequence (one after another) rather than simultaneously. While this approach can address all aspects of building performance, the main challenge is that it requires careful coordination between different building systems to avoid rework. 

This is because decisions made early in the sequence can affect systems designed later, and if not properly coordinated, may require going back to modify earlier work - hence the need to "avoid rework."

In contrast:
- Integrated project delivery (option A) involves all parties working collaboratively from the start, which inherently reduces coordination issues and rework
- "Noncompound" (option B) is not a standard project delivery method term

Sequential delivery matches the description of being concerned with building performance while still facing coordination challenges.
